transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vokoman.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv
overnight.
Yesterday, Ukraine hit Russia's former imperial capital, St. Petersburg, with about 1,000 drones.
One person was killed.
It's Russia that launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but impairs Charles Maine's reports
President Trump is demanding Ukraine stop hitting Russian energy sites.
Trump seems to be trying to protect Russian oil facilities.
Following a deal he cut with President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel, a move Trump
hopes will bring down the price of gas for U.S. voters ahead of midterm elections.
So, in that sense, the news of Ukraine striking energy facilities in St. Petersburg Sunday
is unlikely to please Trump, who's already called previous strikes, including one against
Moscow last week at disgrace.
President Piers Charles Maine's reporting.
President Trump is traveling to central Kansas today for a rally to support Republican Senator
Roger Marshall.
From member station KMUW MAG BRITAIN MELISH reports, the Senate race has become a surprising
toss-up.
The president is set to headline a rally at the 6,500-seat Heartland Credit Union Arena
just north of Wichita.
Trump announced the Kansas stop last week, as polls showed Republican Senator Roger Marshall
tied or falling slightly behind his Democratic challenger, Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor.
Both parties have redirected tens of millions of dollars in recent weeks to try and shape
the race.
Kansas voters have not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932.
Marshall is an avid supporter of the Trump administration and has defended its handling
of tariffs in the war in Iran.
For NPR News, I'm Meg Brittain Melish in Wichita, Kansas.
President Trump has endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election.
Trump is citing Netanyahu's support for the ongoing war against Iran.
Canadian military officials say a fire has killed four Canadian soldiers and badly wounded
another 39 this weekend.
This happened during a fire-related training incident at a base in Alberta.
Dan Carpentzuk reports.
Major General L.W. Rutland says officials at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright were aware
of a grass fire for several hours before it quickly spread to the training area where
training activities were underway.
He says the fire was about three-quarters of a mile from the troops, but because of
what he described as uncommonly strong winds, it reached the exercise area in less than
a minute.
The Defense Department says there are no indications that this was a terrorist attack.
Rutland says there will be a board of inquiry, but because of the number of casualties and
complexities it could take some time.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the nation is in mourning after what he called one of
the worst tragedies for the Canadian military in peacetime.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carpentzuk in Toronto.
This is NPR.
Police in Washington, D.C. say a National Guard member has been shot and wounded in
the leg.
The D.C. police chief says the guard member was with several other troops as they tried
to break up a fight among a group of people on a sidewalk.
The chief says a suspect shot and injured the guard member, and other guard members
opened fire, wounding the suspect.
None of the injuries is life-threatening.
Teens who become addicted to social media are more likely to develop symptoms of depression,
and teens with depression are more likely to become addicted to social media.
NPR's Retude Chatterjee reports on a new study published in the journal Pediatrics.
The findings come from analyzing data on more than 11,000 teenagers.
Researchers followed these teens over five years as part of the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive
Development study.
They assess the teenagers' mental health annually using standardized questionnaires
on symptoms of anxiety and depression, and they assess them for symptoms of social media
addiction.
Pediatrician Dr. Jason Nagata is at the University of California San Francisco and an author
of the new study.
"Addictive social media use and depression can create a vicious cycle for some teenagers
where they kind of reinforce one another and can exacerbate each other's symptoms."
The study did not find a similar relationship between social media addiction and anxiety.
Retude Chatterjee, NPR News.
Pope Leo gave his regular Sunday blessing yesterday in public at the Vatican.
It's been less than a week since he was hospitalized for cancer surgery, a half-part of a lung removed.
The pontiff was discharged on Saturday.
This is NPR.
